O.outcome_detail: final surgical technical performance scores, primarily OSATS

cells.quote: Overall, the average performance scores for VBC were significantly higher than the controls, with a SMD of 0.71 (95% CI 0.37, 1.04, Z = 4.15, p < 0.0001, and Figure 3).
cells.note: Pooled result from nine RCTs including 94 VBC and 89 control participants; the included studies covered undergraduate trainees and surgical residents, simulated and live-surgery tasks, and varied coaching-session schedules.

D.treatment: VBC sessions of 20 minutes or longer

O.outcome_detail: statistically significant improvement in surgical technical performance

cells.quote: Only one of the six studies that included VBC sessions of 20 min or longer failed to show a statistically significant benefit of VBC to the control, whereas three of the four studies that used shorter than 20 min sessions failed to show a significant difference. Therefore, it is likely that the optimum session length is over 20 min, but further studies are required to confirm this.
cells.note: Narrative comparison of session-length subgroups; no direct pooled effect size for session length was reported.

O.outcome_detail: change in surgical technical performance from baseline to final assessment

cells.quote: The overall change in performance from the baseline to final assessment was significantly higher in the VBC group compared to the control, with a SMD of 0.98 (95% CI 0.61, 1.35, Z = 5.19, and p < 0.0001, and Figure 3).
cells.note: Pooled meta-analysis of 10 studies including 137 VBC and 132 control participants; included studies varied in trainee level, simulated versus live surgery, and coaching duration.

O.outcome_detail: final technical performance scores
